newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit up on commercial dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit up on commercial dlr sales.

text.p: * Malaysian ringgit gains on commercial dollar selling by KL parties, underpinned by firm swaps.
* Thai baht eases in offshore market, hovers in narrow range in onshore market as central bank directive to domestic banks not to lend short-term baht funds to overseas players remains.
* Indonesian rupiah largely steady with Jakarta players out for holiday but showing slight upside as market long on dollars.
* Singapore dollar sandwiched in range.
The Malaysian ringgit gained from commercial dollar sales by Kuala Lumpur players on Thursday and dealers said the currency showed more upside potential.
"There is heavy (dollar) selling pressure this morning. Dollar/ringgit could test 2.4900," a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur said.
Apart from demand from Malaysian corporates, he said there was also some early unwinding of long dollar/ringgit positions by overseas funds.
"About $100-150 (million) were sold above the 2.5000 ringgit level by KL parties this morning. So that depressed the market a bit," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.

He said the selling appeared to be for commercial purposes but that players tended to speculate on possible central bank intervention at any aggressive dollar sales by KL banks after Bank Negara's moves last week to squeeze out speculators.

"It's difficult to pinpoint, but I don't think Bank Negara would be interested in intervening at the 2.5000 level. They might start getting uncomfortable if dollar/ringgit went above 2.5100," he said.
Dealers said the continued firm tone of short-dated swaps was also supporting the ringgit.
The European bank dealer said the ringgit faced some resistance around 2.4950 as U.S. funds and short-term interbank players were interested in picking up dollars near that level.
Elsewhere, the Thai baht eased in offshore markets as dollar sales by hedge funds abated, but the currency continued to trade at a large discount to the onshore market.

The baht was quoted at 25.550/25.650 to the dollar at 0430 GMT in the offshore market against 25.080/25.180 baht late on Wednesday. But on the local market, the baht was quoted around 25.770/25.790 against 25.700/25.750 baht late on Wednesday.
The central bank set the midrate on Thursday at 25.75 baht to the dollar versus 25.71 on Wednesday.

The Bank of Thailand (BOT)'s directive to commercial banks not to offer short-term baht funds to foreign buyers following speculative attacks on the baht last week has created two dollar/baht rates for offshore and onshore markets.
Dealers said the move had sharply tightened baht supply in the offshore market where the Thai unit was being traded above the midrate and above the level in the local market.
But it also provided necessary liquidity to the local market to ensure Thai businesses would not be short of cash.
"The local market is calm. The central bank informed us that the measure will be temporary and we don't know how long it will last," a dealer with a foreign bank in Bangkok said.
"However, we are not affected as the central bank allows us to raise funds by bidding swaps with it," she added.
There was market talk the BOT may be working on measures to curb speculation in the future and that an outright ban on offshore access to baht could be imposed, dealers said.
A Singapore-based dealer said the liquidation of long dollar positions by overseas players appeared to have died down.
"It looks like those hedge funds which were caught out have got some of their baht through the spot market so they're not in a hurry to liquidate their long positions now," he said.
The market was also pricing in a cut in the central bank's discount rate amid widespread speculation that such a move was likely, he added.
"The longer dated swaps are coming off across the board. The short dates still look firm but they should ease by month end," he said.
He said the one-month swap rate was likely to head back towards 25/30 while the six-month rate should revisit 35/40.
The Indonesian rupiah was largely steady with Jakarta players out for a holiday, but Singapore dealers said the unit showed a slight upside bias as the market was long on dollars.
"There are (foreign) offers above the 2,445.0 level and Jakarta corporates have interest to sell dollars there too," the European bank dealer said.

He added that the dollar would be supported around the 2,438.0 level due to uncertainty ahead of the May 29 general election. The rupiah was at 2,440.0/42.0 at 0430 GMT against 2,443.25/44.00 late on Wednesday.
The Singapore dollar was sandwiched between commercial demand for the U.S. dollar below the 1.4300 level and selling interest from interbank players above 1.4350.
Dealers said it was likely to hover in a 1.4290-1.4340 band.
-- Madhav Reddy in KL (603-201 4813), Anchalee Koetsawang in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
